cases.title: Real data: QuidelOrtho (QDEL), net debt 6.1x EBITDA
reasons: Kill criterion met: net debt/EBITDA is 6.09x in the data (debt 3,076m, cash 123m, EBITDA 485m), above the 4x threshold. The figure comes from the code-computed dataset, not from the judge. This alone makes it a Reject.

Segment fits: immunoassay and point-of-care diagnostics (instruments, assays) are in-vitro diagnostics. The business is probably consumables-heavy, but the dataset has no recurring-revenue share, so the business-model warning is unverified.

Profitability is mixed. LTM EBITDA margin is 18.1%, but reported fiscal-year EBITDA was -1,490m in 2024 and -483m in 2025. That points to large impairments or one-offs, and the dataset doesn't explain them. Revenue also fell from 2,998m (2023) to 2,730m (2025), about -9% over two years.

Why the price is low is unknown. The share price is down 54% over 12 months and 22% over 3 months. The dataset has no cause, and the headlines only say shares 'plummeted' after Q2. Temporary versus structural can't be shown, so this would be Radar at best even without the leverage issue.

Ownership: no holder is above 25%. The largest are BlackRock 16.3%, FMR 10.7% and Newtyn Management 9.7%, and insiders hold 0.9%. No ownership flag is raised and there is no controlling-shareholder issue. Newtyn is an activist-style holder, but nothing says it has made a public statement about a sale.
Regulatory: the dataset has no information on regulatory matters, so this is unknown rather than clear.

Financing angle: leverage of over 6x EBITDA leaves little room for an LBO structure. Market cap is EUR 790m against EV of EUR 3.4bn, so debt is the larger part of the capital structure. A take-private would need most of the existing debt refinanced or assumed, which conflicts with the thesis of funding the next product cycle and add-ons.
Conclusion: the kill criterion on leverage is mechanically met, so Reject. Re-check only if net debt/EBITDA falls below 4x, for example through deleveraging or an equity-heavy deal.
